blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Between June 2026 and October 2026, detached houses: listings fell from 86 in June to 81 in October (−5.8%), and it took 3.0% of the city’s 464 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings fell from 618 in June to 604 in October (−2.3%), and it took 34.1% of the city’s 737 sales over the period.
The monthly write-ups singled out Whalley for detached houses in June, July, October (a buyers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in July, September, October (a buyers’ best bet).

items.t: Bear Creek Green Timbers real estate

Whalley is the City community and "City Centre" is its downtown core — the City lists the community as "City Centre (Whalley)," and downtown addresses sit around King George Boulevard, City Parkway and 104 Avenue.

The board's name for this ground is Whalley, not Surrey City Centre: board reporting for Surrey carries a Whalley sub-area and no City Centre sub-area, so listings and statistics for the downtown are filed under Whalley. (SnapStats, September 2026)
Guildford is east of Whalley, Newton is south, and Bridgeview and the Fraser River are north, with Scott Road and North Delta to the west.
The core's stock is strata condominiums in concrete towers at the stations, with mid-rise and townhouse product at the core's edges and older single-detached houses on the surrounding Whalley blocks.

King George Hub, at King George Station, is the named master-planned cluster on the south end of the core: its residential towers are Hub One (13615 Fraser Hwy), Hub Two (13655 Fraser Hwy), The Line rental tower (13639 George Junction) and Plaza One & Two (13725 & 13745 George Junction), by PCI Developments.
Two building waves define the area: 1970s-era low-rise rental and detached stock outside the core, and post-2000 tower construction inside it that accelerated after the 2017 City Centre Plan.
Central City, 13450 102 Avenue, is the core's landmark mixed complex — shopping centre, office tower and Simon Fraser University's Surrey campus stacked over Surrey Central Station.

What can be built beside a Whalley home is set by the City Centre Plan, approved in 2017 and now under update: the update establishes a Central Business District, identifies a future Entertainment District, enables more transit-oriented development around SkyTrain stations and allows growth in Bolivar Heights.

blocks.text: Whalley: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Simon Fraser University's Surrey campus is inside the Central City shopping centre at 250 - 13450 102 Avenue, next to Surrey Central Station; its first building opened above the mall in fall 2006 and was designed by architect Bing Thom.
Kwantlen Polytechnic University also has a Civic Plaza campus in the core, and Surrey City Hall and the City Centre Library (10350 University Drive) complete the civic cluster around the stations.
Holland Park, 13428 Old Yale Road, is the downtown's central green space and festival site at 10 hectares.
Chuck Bailey Recreation Centre, 13458 107A Avenue, is the core's recreation centre, and the City is expanding it.

Central City shopping centre, 10153 King George Blvd, is anchored by T&T Supermarket, Winners, Shoppers Drug Mart and Walmart — the core's full-service grocery anchor is a mall tenant, not a standalone store.

SFU Stephens Family School of Medicine, Centre Block (SFU / Province of BC) — permanent home in Surrey City Centre adjacent to SFU Surrey and Surrey Central SkyTrain Station, occupying eight floors of a 12-storey building with a 49-space child care centre; the first class of 48 students began at the interim SFU Surrey Central building in August 2026; status: permanent home opening fall 2030, construction anticipated late 2026 (as of November 3, 2026).

Regency Gardens redevelopment (Onni) — multi-phase redevelopment of the Regency Gardens site at 10520 132 St / 105–105A Ave; status: active application No. 7924-0084-00 being processed by the City under the City Centre framework (planning report dated February 23, 2026) (as of November 3, 2026).

City Centre Arena and Entertainment District (City of Surrey) — in October 2025 Council endorsed creating an Entertainment District in City Centre, and the City is running a process to select a partner for a City Centre arena within it; status: partner-selection process underway (as of November 3, 2026).

PARKWAY (Bosa Properties) — four-tower masterplan at 10460 City Pkwy, following the completed two-tower University District at 104 Ave and University Dr (North Tower, 13428 105 Ave; South Tower, 10448 University Dr, completed 2023); status: PARKWAY under construction per the developer (as of November 3, 2026).

City Centre Plan update (City of Surrey) — adds the Central Business District and Entertainment District and more transit-oriented development around stations; status: update underway (as of November 3, 2026).
Surrey property taxes are due July 2, with a 5% penalty if not paid by midnight July 2 and a further 5% penalty after September 2.
Whalley holds all four of Surrey's Expo Line stations — Scott Road, Gateway, Surrey Central and King George — making it the only Surrey community on the SkyTrain network today.
The R1 King George Blvd RapidBus runs from Newton Exchange to Guildford Exchange via Surrey Central Station and King George Station, so both ends of the core have a rapid-bus spine as well as rail.
Route 321 links Surrey Central Station south along King George Boulevard through King George Station toward Newton Exchange and White Rock Centre.

The Surrey Langley SkyTrain extends the Expo Line east from King George Station along Fraser Highway, with an anticipated in-service date of 2029 — King George stays the transfer point between the two lines' Surrey segments.

The core's main due-diligence layer is the plan, not a hazard map: the City Centre Plan update is redrawing districts around the stations, so check a parcel's current and proposed designation in COSMOS and the plan update before valuing redevelopment potential.

For strata towers, the plan pages do not state a building's rental or pet bylaws, depreciation report position or special levies — those come only from the strata's own documents for the specific building.

faq.q: Is Whalley the same place as Surrey City Centre?
faq.a: City Centre is the downtown core inside the larger Whalley community. The City lists it as "City Centre (Whalley)," one of its communities, while the real estate board's sub-area name for the whole area is Whalley. A buyer searching only "City Centre" will miss board data and listings filed under Whalley.

Four Expo Line stations, and they are the only SkyTrain stations in Surrey: Scott Road, Gateway, Surrey Central and King George. Surrey Central and King George anchor the City Centre core itself; Gateway and Scott Road serve the wider Whalley blocks to the north. The R1 King George Blvd RapidBus also runs through the core between Newton Exchange and Guildford Exchange.

faq.q: Which schools serve a City Centre address?
faq.a: The in-area public schools are A.H.P. Matthew Elementary and Queen Elizabeth Secondary, so run the exact address before relying on a school.

faq.q: Is downtown Whalley in a floodplain?
faq.a: No area-specific flood regime applies to the core. City Centre is upland, away from Surrey's floodplain lowlands, which the City places along the Nicomekl and Serpentine Rivers toward Cloverdale and Newton and on the Little Campbell River in the south. The core is also outside the Agricultural Land Reserve. Confirm any single parcel in COSMOS.
